clue.text: 18 and perfect, spurning fellow

definitions.note: the cross-reference points to the answer at 18-across, a word meaning without regulation

indicators.note: spurning means rejecting, so the letter for fellow is thrown out of the word for perfect

parts.note: perfect means flawless, without a single fault

explanation.surface: A description of someone ideal who refuses company, with a cross-reference to make it puzzling.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the answer to 18-across, ANARCHIC; take F (fellow) away from FLAWLESS.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonyms: a state without rules or order can be called anarchic or lawless interchangeably.

clue.text: Deity's associate upheld as devoted character

indicators.note: upheld means held up, which in a down light reads the pieces upwards

parts.note: a deity is a god
a pal is an associate, a friend

explanation.surface: A god's companion raised up as a loyal figure.
explanation.walkthrough: GOD + PAL read upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Metaphor: a person who slavishly follows and serves another, like a pampered pet dog.

clue.text: Endless drink leads to hesitation? The smallest amount

indicators.note: endless means without its last letter, so the spirit loses its tail

parts.note: whisky is a drink
er is a hesitating sound; 'leads to' just sets it after the drink

explanation.surface: Drinking too much makes a person hesitate.
explanation.walkthrough: WHISKY loses its Y, then ER.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: winning by a hair's breadth is winning by a very small margin, a tiny amount.

clue.text: Still not cut up

definitions.meaning: still as an intensifier, as in 'still better' or 'yet better'
not cut up means not upset, staying calm and level

explanation.surface: Something remaining whole and unsliced.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: an adverb for emphasis like 'yet', and an adjective meaning calm or smooth-tempered.

clue.text: Tar storage unit containing a last bit of tar

indicators.note: containing means holding inside, so the storage unit takes in the a

parts.note: a silo is a storage unit for grain

indicators.note: last bit of picks the final letter of the word tar

explanation.surface: A storage tank that holds tar, plus a little more of it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tar' at the start is the definition, an old word for a seaman, not the black substance.
explanation.definitionFit: Crossword-favourite slang: a tar or jack tar is a seaman, from tarpaulin.

clue.text: Information is found about bridge opponents for a start

indicators.note: about here means going round, so the first pieces surround the bridge pair

parts.note: gen is British slang for information
in bridge East and South sit next to each other and play against one another

explanation.surface: Someone gathering intelligence on their bridge rivals before play begins.
explanation.walkthrough: In bridge, North-South partner against East-West, so East and South are opponents. 'for' is only a link to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Genesis means an origin or beginning, and is also the first book of the Bible.

clue.text: Pay for nothing, investing in newspaper? Just the reverse — overindulge

indicators.note: after building the wordplay, the whole thing is read the other way round
investing in means putting inside, so the payment and nothing go into the newspaper

parts.note: a rag is a disparaging word for a newspaper
to foot the bill is to pay for it
nothing is zero, the letter O

explanation.surface: Paying nothing to invest in a paper, then the opposite, and going overboard.
explanation.walkthrough: The container builds RAFOOTOG; 'Just the reverse' then reads the whole of it backwards, rather than swapping which piece holds which.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiomatic phrase: to exceed reasonable limits, to overdo things.

clue.text: Note few at sea went fishing in a modern way

definitions.note: an adverbial phrase standing for an adjective meaning modern

indicators.note: at sea means confused, so the three letters are scrambled

parts.note: angled means went fishing with rod and line

explanation.surface: A note recording how a few people went fishing with new techniques.
explanation.walkthrough: N + EWF (an anagram of FEW) + ANGLED.
explanation.definitionFit: Paraphrase: describes something novel, often disparagingly, as modern gimmickry.

clue.text: Dog's range: that is a short length

parts.note: a span is a range
L is the short form of length

explanation.surface: How far a dog can roam, measured briefly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dog's' is 'Dog is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a breed of gundog with long ears and silky coat.

clue.text: Special quality of beer-barrel, say, in seaside resort

parts.note: a keg is a beer-barrel
the suffix -ness forms nouns meaning the quality of something

explanation.surface: The special qualities of beer at a seaside town.
explanation.walkthrough: SKEGNESS is a seaside resort on the Lincolnshire coast of England.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a classic English holiday town on the Lincolnshire coast, famous for its 'bracing' slogan.

clue.text: Police riots harshly, repeatedly omitting nothing in charge-sheet?

indicators.note: the riots are handled roughly, so the letters of the two words are thrown into a new order
omitting means leaving out, so letters are removed from the police riots fodder
repeatedly says the omission happens twice, once for each round letter

parts.note: nothing is zero, the letter O

explanation.surface: Police dealing roughly with riots and charging people, all written up on a charge-sheet.
explanation.walkthrough: POLICE RIOTS has two Os; 'repeatedly omitting nothing' strikes both, leaving PLICERITS to rearrange. The question mark admits the pun: a list of prices is a sheet of charges.
explanation.definitionFit: A pun: a tariff showing what is charged for each item is literally a sheet of charges.

clue.text: How baleen may be represented?

parts.note: baleen is the horny filtering plates in a large sea mammal's mouth, commonly described by a two-part compound name

explanation.surface: A question about how a zoological term might be described or depicted.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer spans 10-across and 26-down; baleen is simply another name for it.
explanation.definitionFit: Equivalent terms: baleen is the flexible plate material from filter-feeding cetaceans, once used for corset stays.

clue.text: Describing wine flavour? Satisfactory to have change of heart

indicators.note: the heart of the word is its middle, and changing it here means its two central letters swap places

parts.note: satisfactory means okay, all right

explanation.surface: A wine judged merely acceptable until the taster changes their mind.
explanation.walkthrough: Swap the middle letters K and A of OKAY.
explanation.definitionFit: Wine aged in barrels takes on a woody taste from the timber, and tasters call that flavour by the tree's name.

clue.text: Sound of surprise about monarch leading country (a role acknowledged here?)

indicators.note: leading means coming first, so the first part goes in front of the country
about means surrounding, so the exclamation goes round the royal letter

parts.note: coo is a British exclamation of surprise
R stands for rex or regina, king or queen
a country is a nation

explanation.surface: An exclamation at a monarch heading the country, the parenthesis hinting at a ceremony.
explanation.walkthrough: COO is a dated British exclamation ('Coo, look at that!'). The definition is the bracketed part: the monarch's role is formally acknowledged at this ceremony.
explanation.definitionFit: Descriptive definition: the crowning ceremony is where a new sovereign's position is formally recognised.

clue.text: Top show, cut, TV men mangled? Avoid

indicators.note: cut means shortened, so the show loses its last letter

parts.note: a circus is a show under the big top

indicators.note: mangled means badly damaged, so the letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: A top TV show cut and mangled, to be avoided.
explanation.walkthrough: CIRCU + MVENT, an anagram of TV MEN.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonyms: to get round or evade a problem or rule.

clue.text: Damage name, being released from arrest

indicators.note: released from means let out of, so the letter for name leaves the word for arrest

parts.note: run in is British informal for arrest, as police run in a suspect

explanation.surface: A wrongly arrested person freed but with their name damaged.
explanation.walkthrough: RUN IN, to arrest, loses an N.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonyms as verbs: to wreck or spoil something is to damage it.

clue.text: Fruit flavour alone recalled

parts.note: a tang is a sharp flavour

indicators.note: recalled is read as called back, so the word for alone is read backwards

parts.note: sole means alone, the only one

explanation.surface: Remembering a taste enjoyed in solitude.
explanation.walkthrough: 'recalled' turns SOLE into ELOS.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a tangelo is a citrus hybrid of tangerine and pomelo or grapefruit.

clue.text: Beat leads to Brasenose College dance being cut

parts.note: to lam is to beat or thrash

indicators.note: leads here are the leading letters of the two college words

parts.note: a hop is an informal dance

explanation.surface: A college dance spoiled by beating.
explanation.walkthrough: Brasenose is an Oxford college. 'Cut' is a cut of meat.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a cut of meat from a young sheep, usually including a rib.

clue.text: Rubbish is in my emptied bedroom (wanting it anywhere but!)

indicators.note: rubbish means trash, signalling the letters are jumbled
emptied means the inside is removed, leaving only the outer letters of bedroom

explanation.surface: Rubbish strewn in someone's bedroom which they want anywhere else.
explanation.walkthrough: Fodder is IS IN MY + BM.
explanation.definitionFit: The 'not in my back yard' attitude: opposing a development near home but not elsewhere.

clue.text: Governed area after revolution, with style, and without regulation

indicators.note: a revolution turns things round, so the governed-area pieces are read backwards

parts.note: governed means ran, as in ran the country
chic means style, elegance

explanation.surface: A political story: a region governed before a revolution, now stylish and lawless.
explanation.walkthrough: RAN + A reversed gives ANAR; then CHIC.
explanation.definitionFit: Paraphrase: something with no rules or order imposed on it is chaotic and ungoverned.

clue.text: Lady-love besotted a Moor with sex appeal

indicators.note: besotted means intoxicated, so the letters are muddled

explanation.surface: A sweetheart charmed by an attractive Moor.
explanation.walkthrough: AMORO (anagram of A MOOR) + SA.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a woman who is loved, a mistress or sweetheart.

clue.text: Beemer clearly can get round it!?

definitions.text: Beemer clearly can get round it!?

indicators.note: the two words get round, that is surround, the answer, which sits inside them

explanation.surface: A boast that a BMW can overtake a rival car.
explanation.walkthrough: Beemer is slang for a BMW. The answer sits in beeMER Clearly, and the whole clue is the definition: a rival German car the BMW literally surrounds.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang abbreviation for a Mercedes-Benz, the Stuttgart luxury marque that is the BMW's chief rival.

clue.text: Cavalryman's dismissal after reduction in expense

indicators.note: after means following, so the dismissal word comes second
reduction means shortened, so the expense word loses its final letter

parts.note: cost means expense
the sack is a dismissal from a job

explanation.surface: A soldier dismissed in a round of cost-cutting.
explanation.walkthrough: COS(T) + SACK.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a member of the Russian horse-riding warrior communities serving as cavalry.

clue.text: Exam sounds harsh when described on the radio

indicators.note: radio is heard not seen, signalling a word that sounds like another

parts.note: these words are said aloud, and what is heard is the sound this part of the answer needs

explanation.surface: An exam that sounds harsh on air.
explanation.walkthrough: Greats is the Oxford finals exam in classics.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the final examinations for the Oxford classics degree.

clue.text: Today's heartless tirade identifying dictator

indicators.note: heartless means losing its middle, so only the outer letters remain

parts.note: the word today, 's just linking it
a rant is a tirade

explanation.surface: A newspaper editorial spots a dictator from a heartless tirade.
explanation.walkthrough: TODAY loses its middle ODA, leaving TY, then RANT.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: an absolute ruler who governs cruelly and oppressively.

clue.text: Hero of novel's to work with sexton in part of London

parts.note: Leopold Bloom is the hero of James Joyce's Ulysses; with the 's he becomes Bloom's
a sexton digs graves, and the work that goes with it is to bury the dead

explanation.surface: A literary hero taking a job alongside a gravedigger in London.
explanation.walkthrough: Bloom is the hero of Joyce's novel Ulysses. A sexton is a church officer who traditionally dug graves.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a district of central London known for the British Museum and its literary group.

clue.text: Women put off by insubstantial game

indicators.note: put off means removed, so the letter for women is taken from the word meaning insubstantial

parts.note: wispy means thin and insubstantial

explanation.surface: Women unimpressed by a flimsy game.
explanation.walkthrough: WISPY loses W.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a children's guessing game played on journeys, naming something beginning with a letter.

clue.text: See 10
English scientist having reasonable skill in garden

indicators.note: in means placed inside, so the term for passable goes inside the gardening word

parts.note: to hoe is to garden, working soil with a hoe
OK means reasonable, passable, as in an OK level of skill

explanation.surface: A scientist who is a reasonably able gardener.
explanation.walkthrough: 'garden' is a verb here, the work done with a hoe, not a plot of land.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: Robert Hooke, 17th-century English natural philosopher famous for his law of elasticity.

clue.text: Lady-love? In an instant scoundrel is in front of one

parts.note: in a mo, short for in a moment, means in an instant
a rat is a scoundrel
A means one

explanation.surface: A sudden romantic cad stepping in front of someone.
explanation.walkthrough: IN A MO is British for 'in a moment'.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: an Italian-derived word for a woman one loves, a female sweetheart.

clue.text: Ghostly Englishman circling most of Hampshire

indicators.note: circling means surrounding, so the Englishman goes round the county

parts.note: Pom is Australian slang for an Englishman

indicators.note: most of means all but the last letter

parts.note: Hants is the standard abbreviation for Hampshire, an English county

explanation.surface: An Englishman travelling round most of Hampshire with an eerie air.
explanation.walkthrough: Hampshire, a county in southern England, is abbreviated HANTS; most of it is HANT. POM is Australian slang for an English person.
explanation.definitionFit: Used as an adjective: spectral, unreal, like an apparition.

clue.text: Like Scottish mouse's position, circling vegetable

indicators.note: circling means surrounding, so the position word goes round the vegetable

parts.note: to sit is to be in a position
a leek is a vegetable

explanation.surface: Where a Scottish mouse sits among the vegetables.
explanation.walkthrough: Robert Burns's poem To a Mouse opens 'Wee, sleekit, cow'rin, tim'rous beastie'.
explanation.definitionFit: Literary allusion: Burns describes the field mouse with this Scots word meaning smooth and glossy.
